rows.decision: The line under the name is: Build for a future audit from the first commit. Because in an audit, every commit counts.
rows.why: An audit reads the history of a product, change by change. So the work for it starts with the first commit, and not in the month before.

rows.decision: A block of the interface is called a component.
rows.why: It is the word that designers and developers search for. The word part is kept for a part of anything else.

rows.decision: Advice about tools is a plugin of its own, and it names a tool only as an example of a kind.
rows.why: Advice gets old faster than the core. A team can then take the page away, or change it, without touching a rule.

rows.decision: The scripts are read by a well-known linter, which lives in a folder of its own with its own packages.
rows.why: A reviewer looks for a linter by name. In its own folder, it adds no package to the build, the check or the site.

rows.decision: A commit and a pull request name the responsible person only, and no tool or AI agent.
rows.why: A person answers for every change. The name of a tool in the record would blur who that is.

rows.decision: A small set of utility classes is the last layer of the stylesheet.
rows.why: A page then never needs a style attribute. The set stays small, so that parts with names carry the design.

rows.decision: The history of the repository is kept as a record, and one command reads every commit.
rows.why: A review of a regulated product reads the history. A mistake that is published cannot be taken back.

rows.decision: A product changes its look in a theme file, and never in the tokens of the core.
rows.why: The core can then be updated, and the check still measures the colours of the product.

rows.decision: Ordinance DS is a base to build on, with components, layout and patterns. It is not a library of finished screens.
rows.why: An organisation and its AI agents build the product. The framework keeps the rules that a test can measure.

rows.decision: Form controls and the dialog are native elements of HTML.
rows.why: The browser then gives them the keyboard, the label and the role, and the page needs no script for them.

rows.decision: The accessibility rules that a script can read are a rule of the check.
rows.why: A missing name or label is then found before a person has to find it.

rows.decision: The framework is named Ordinance DS.
rows.why: The first product takes the name Ordinance. Two things with one name would be mixed up.

rows.decision: Version control starts in the folder, with no remote copy.
rows.why: The history is then kept from the first day, and nothing is published before the owner decides.

rows.decision: Under the strict security policy, Base UI components are rendered in the browser.
rows.why: On a server, Base UI writes style attributes, and the policy blocks them.

rows.decision: The licence of Ordinance DS is MIT.
rows.why: It is short and well known, and it lets a team use the framework in a closed product.

rows.decision: The pages are in English only, and the build can add a language.
rows.why: One language keeps the texts true. A team that needs another language adds files and changes no code.

rows.decision: The icons are Heroicons, as files in the folder.
rows.why: The set is open, under the MIT licence. The build puts an icon into the page, so no request is made for it.

rows.decision: The typefaces are Noto Sans, Noto Serif and Noto Sans Mono, as files in the folder.
rows.why: One open family covers the three roles and many scripts. The pages ask no other server.

rows.decision: Typefaces are the system's own until files are chosen. Replaced by D-14.
rows.why: A page that downloads no typeface is the fastest and the most private.

rows.decision: A page says checked only for a rule in the check.
rows.why: A statement that nothing checks becomes false without anyone seeing it.

rows.decision: Names of other products are held as hashes.
rows.why: The check can refuse a name without containing it.

rows.decision: What is left out is left out everywhere.
rows.why: A half-removed part leaves names and pages that nobody owns.

rows.decision: Hiding items of the menu for a plan or a role is not in the core.
rows.why: Hiding in the browser protects nothing, and it can look like access control.

rows.decision: The first version has no gateway for data.
rows.why: A gateway that is half built would be the weakest part. The page Data lists what a gateway must do.

rows.decision: A plugin is compiled in, and never loaded while the site runs.
rows.why: Code that arrives while the site runs cannot be reviewed or listed first.

rows.decision: The menu and the help open without a script.
rows.why: They are the parts that every reader needs, so they must not depend on a script.

rows.decision: Tokens follow the Design Tokens format.
rows.why: A shared format lets other tools read the tokens.

rows.decision: A state is an attribute, never a class.
rows.why: Plain HTML and component frameworks can then share one stylesheet.

rows.decision: Classes are named as block, element and modifier.
rows.why: A name then shows what a part belongs to.

rows.decision: Every name is registered before it is used.
rows.why: The check can then find a name that is wrong, and a name that nothing uses.

rows.decision: The build and the checks have no dependency.
rows.why: Every dependency is a file from others that someone must watch.
